To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

oscillatory strains applied during contraction reduce the maximal velocity and power of trachealis muscle, whereas oscillatory strains applied in the absence of activation have no effect on these properties.

the force-velocity properties change in trachealis after imposition of length changes in both the relaxed and activated states, and the changes are consistent with the hypothesis that the contractile filams are disrupted by the imposed oscillations.

the oscillatory strains imposed during the relaxation phase caused the force-velocity relationship to shift to a higher level, whereas oscillation applied during activation caused the force- velocity relationship to shift to the left and down.

the effect of the dynamic environment on the contractility of airway smooth muscles.
the effects of oscillation on contractile function of trachealis muscle, with the aim of understanding the mechanism by which the mechanical properties of smooth muscle are altered in vivo.
the dynamic nature of the lung and the effects of oscillation on the contractile apparatus of airway smooth muscles.
